\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مظاهرة} (muẓāhara)}{مظاهرة (muẓāhara)}]{\ar{مظاهرة} (muẓāhara) — a demonstration, a march}

\label{lesson:AR-C353-muzahara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a commotion, then the Arabic for a crowd.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مظاهرة}}
\textbf{\ar{مظاهرة}} — \emph{muẓāhara} — \textquotedblleft{}a demonstration, a march\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سار} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{في} \ar{مظاهرة} \ar{سلمية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāra aṭ-ṭullāb fī muẓāhara silmiyya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students walked in a peaceful march.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مظاهرة}} (\emph{muẓāhara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ẓ-h-r} (Lane), the root of \emph{ẓahr}, the back, and \emph{ẓahara}, to appear. Form III \emph{ẓāhara} is \textquotedblleft{}to back someone up\textquotedblright{}; a public show of support is the modern sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muẓāhara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muẓāhara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāra aṭ-ṭullāb fī muẓāhara silmiyya.} — The students walked in a peaceful march.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a commotion, then the Arabic for a crowd, then say \emph{muẓāhara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مظاهرة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A demonstration, a march\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تجمع} (tajammaʿa)}{تجمع (tajammaʿa)}]{\ar{تجمع} (tajammaʿa) — to gather, to assemble}

\label{lesson:AR-C353-tajammaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a crowd, then the Arabic for a demonstration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تجمع}}
\textbf{\ar{تجمع}} — \emph{tajammaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to gather, to assemble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تجمع} \ar{الناس} \ar{حول} \ar{السيارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tajammaʿa an-nās ḥawla as-sayyāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People gathered round the car.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتجمع}, \emph{yatajammaʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تجمع}} (\emph{tajammaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-m-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to gather\textquotedblright{} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{ijtimāʿ}, a meeting. It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to come together\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tajammaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tajammaʿa an-nās ḥawla as-sayyāra.} — People gathered round the car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a crowd, then the Arabic for a demonstration, then say \emph{tajammaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{هتف} (hatafa)}{هتف (hatafa)}]{\ar{هتف} (hatafa) — to cheer, to chant}

\label{lesson:AR-C353-hatafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a demonstration, then the Arabic for to gather.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{هتف}}
\textbf{\ar{هتف}} — \emph{hatafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to cheer, to chant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هتف} \ar{الأطفال} \ar{فرحا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hatafa al-aṭfāl faraḥan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children cheered for joy.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهتف}, \emph{yahtif}.

The taught \ar{هاتف}, a telephone, is the same root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{هتف}} (\emph{hatafa}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{h-t-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to call out\textquotedblright{}, where \emph{hātif} was a voice heard when the speaker is not seen; modern Arabic gave that word the telephone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hatafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hatafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hatafa al-aṭfāl faraḥan.} — The children cheered for joy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a demonstration, then the Arabic for to gather, then say \emph{hatafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اقتحم} (iqtaḥama)}{اقتحم (iqtaḥama)}]{\ar{اقتحم} (iqtaḥama) — to break into, to storm}

\label{lesson:AR-C353-iqtahama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to gather, then the Arabic for to cheer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اقتحم}}
\textbf{\ar{اقتحم}} — \emph{iqtaḥama} — \textquotedblleft{}to break into, to storm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اقتحمت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{البيت} \ar{في} \ar{الصباح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iqtaḥamat ash-shurṭa al-bayt fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police stormed the house in the morning.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقتحم}, \emph{yaqtaḥim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اقتحم}} (\emph{iqtaḥama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-ḥ-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to rush into a thing without thought\textquotedblright{}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to force one's way in\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انتشر} (intashara)}{انتشر (intashara)}]{\ar{انتشر} (intashara) — to spread}

\label{lesson:AR-C353-intashara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to cheer, then the Arabic for to break into.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انتشر}}
\textbf{\ar{انتشر}} — \emph{intashara} — \textquotedblleft{}to spread\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتشر} \ar{الخبر} \ar{في} \ar{القرية} \ar{بسرعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intashara al-khabar fī al-qarya bi-surʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The news spread through the village quickly.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينتشر}, \emph{yantashir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انتشر}} (\emph{intashara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-sh-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to spread out\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{nashara}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to spread itself\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
